properties.name: The root-cause rule is served to every project, and a plain get_instructions returns the whole document again
properties.rationale: Root cause: fact:a-cause-written-in-a-reply-is-seen-by-nothing-and-the-root-cause-rule-was-served-to-no-consumer-2026-10-06. The rule lived only in reflow2's contributor AGENTS.md, so the hub, Alex's projects and every flo2.io design never received it, and a cause written in a reply calls no tool any detector could see. Fixing the delivery exposed a second defect in the path itself (fact:a-plain-get-instructions-withheld-the-whole-document-from-v0-78-0-and-the-pin-that-would-have-caught-it-was-never-committed-2026-10-06): since v0.78.0 a plain get_instructions withheld the whole document, so a rule added there would never have arrived. Anthony chose "No limit by default" over moving the 7.3 KB tool inventory to a fetched section or trimming to fit, because either of those hits the same wall at the next addition. He kept the Stop-hook detector closed ("leave the hook closed"). What still cannot be caught is a cause written in a reply by an agent that ignores a delivered rule; the 09-18 miss happened where rule 10 was loaded.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: The two-tier root-cause rule (search the exact error on any failure; get_skill root-cause the moment a cause is about to be written, in the design or in a reply) is now in the served instructions as a standing section near the top, in one handshake sentence that ends before character 1,200, and in the VS Code route's always-loaded file. get_instructions no longer applies the shared 30,000 reply default: a plain call returns the whole document, and only a caller that names its cap gets the manifest instead. tools/replies_are_bounded.py's reviewed exemption says so.
